## 3. New public API

```rust
/// The model turn did not end cleanly (`Length` or `ContentFilter`), so the
/// loop did not run its tool calls.
#[error("tool calls not run: the model turn ended with {finish_reason:?} ({})", capped_names(tool_names))]
#[non_exhaustive]
ToolCallsNotRun {
    /// Why the model turn stopped. `None` when the stream ended with no
    /// `Finish` event (see §10.2).
    finish_reason: Option<FinishReason>,
    /// The names of the tool calls that did not run, in item order (core
    /// sorts tool calls by `call_id`).
    tool_names: Vec<String>,
},
```

- `AgentError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant is an additive change.
  No crate outside core matches `AgentError` without a wildcard.
- The variant is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a later `call_ids`, `usage` or
| `guardrail_intervened` | LiteLLM | `Other` | `ContentFilter` | [L] maps it to `content_filter`; accept the raw value too. Decided in the brief. |
| any other value | LiteLLM | `Other` | `Other` | [L]: the proxy maps every vendor value to the five OpenAI values and maps an unknown value to `stop`. |

This changes a public value (`ModelTurn::finish_reason`) for those stop
reasons. Each touched provider crate gets an upgrade note in its CHANGELOG.

### 10.2 A stream that ends with no `Finish`

Today `ModelTurnAccumulator` sets `Stop` when no `Finish` comes, so a stream
that the server closes early can run a named call with `{}`.

Rule: the accumulator records whether it saw a `Finish`. When `finish()` runs
with one or more tool calls and no `Finish` was seen, it returns `Err` (a
reassembly error). The local driver maps this error to
`AgentError::ToolCallsNotRun { finish_reason: None, .. }` through the §2.2
path. A turn with no tool calls and no `Finish` keeps today's behavior
(`Stop`).

Why this shape (my call): it adds no field to `ModelTurn` or to
`TransitionInput::ModelResponse`, so there is no breaking change and no
Temporal payload change. On Temporal, the `call_model` activity fails with the
error; its result is in the history, so replay does not change.

Risk: a test mock or a provider that sends tool calls with no `Finish` now
fails. The builder finds each such site and fixes the mock or the provider.
The `Model::invoke` contract already requires `Finish` when a stop reason was
seen.

Tests: an accumulator unit test (tool call, no `Finish` → `Err`; text only, no
`Finish` → `Ok` with `Stop`), and an end-to-end driver test (`MockTool` not
invoked, `ToolCallsNotRun { finish_reason: None, .. }`).

### Spec Compliance
**Verdict: compliant with spec §10.2 and the brief.** The following items match the spec and the brief:
- The `finish_seen` field is set in `observe` (crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:741).
- The public getter `finish_seen()` has a `///` doc comment (model.rs:762-767).
- `finish()` returns `Err` when the turn has tool calls and no `Finish`, and the error names the calls through `cap_names` (model.rs:796-811).
- The driver reads `finish_seen()` before `finish()` consumes `acc`. The no-Finish check comes first, then the Length/ContentFilter check, then `Other` (crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:1508-1539).
- The CHANGELOG bullet matches the brief word for word (crates/paigasus-helikon-core/CHANGELOG.md:15).
- The book has the extra sentence (docs/book/src/concepts/agent-loop.md:51).
- No real provider source code changed.

I found one behavior gap that the spec does not cover. A user cancel now gives the wrong error (see Important).

### Mutation check result
I changed model.rs:796 to `if false && !self.finish_seen && ...` by hand and ran both commands in the foreground:
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core --lib no_finish`: `no_finish_with_tool_call_is_an_error` **FAILED**. The turn returned `Ok`, with `finish_reason: Stop` and args `{}`. `no_finish_text_only_still_stop` passed, which is correct because it is the control case.
- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-core --test tool_calls_not_run stream_without_finish`: `stream_without_finish_runs_no_tool` **FAILED** at `assert!(tool.invocations().is_empty())`, because the tool ran.

I put the line back by hand. After that, `git diff --stat` and `git status --short` are empty and HEAD is 50734f6d. The new tests reach the new code, so the missing RED run is not a problem now.

I also ran the tests at HEAD for core, the five providers, evals, cli, runtime-tokio and runtime-temporal with `--all-features --no-fail-fast -- --skip trybuild`. Result: 1986 passed, 0 failed. `trybuild_ui` fails at HEAD, and the implementer says it also fails before the change (a rustc 1.99 drift). I did not run it on the base commit.

### Provider audit
| provider | Finish emitted on normal end? | file:line | SAFE/AT RISK |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | Yes. `message_delta.stop_reason` is held until `message_stop`, then `terminal_events` sends it. A clean EOF without `message_stop` also flushes it. A refusal or a "both tools" case gives `Err`, not `Finish`. | providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:258-263, 397-410; model.rs:118-124 | SAFE |
| Bedrock | Yes. `MessageStop` is held until `Metadata` arrives (in either order), and EOF flushes a held reason. A refused tool call already ended the stream with `Err`. | providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:283-311, 335-340; model.rs:154-161 | SAFE |
| Gemini | Yes. `finishReason` is taken from any candidate chunk, also the last one. `finish()` runs on EOF and on `[DONE]`. Without a `finishReason` it sends no `Finish`, which is the truncation case. An SSE payload that does not parse is skipped (`continue`); if that payload was the last chunk, the turn now fails, which is correct. | providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:79-80, 97-120; model.rs:149-157 | SAFE |
| LiteLLM | Yes, when the proxy sends a `finish_reason`, and the proxy always sends one. `finish()` runs on EOF and on `[DONE]`. | providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:371-374, 739-757; model.rs:154-164 | SAFE |
| OpenAI chat | Yes, when a `finish_reason` arrived. The value is held and sent in `finish()` at EOF, and async-openai uses `[DONE]` itself. Without one, it deliberately sends no `Finish` (debug log). Small extra risk: `base_url` exists for vLLM and other compatible servers (builder.rs:72-76). A non-conforming server that never sends `finish_reason` now fails every tool turn. vLLM, Ollama and llama.cpp do send one. | providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:77-84, 369-390, 520-529 | SAFE (conforming servers) |
| OpenAI Responses | Yes. `terminal_events` always adds `Finish` on `response.completed` and `response.incomplete`. A stream that ends before those events sends none, which is truncation. | providers-openai/src/backend/responses.rs:655-692, 762-795; :71 | SAFE |
| RetryingModel (runtime-tokio) | Passes every event through unchanged. | runtime-tokio/src/retry.rs:217-230 | SAFE |
| CliModel | Delegates to OpenAI, Anthropic or Mock. | cli/src/model.rs:37-49 | SAFE |
| evals MockModel (public) | Replays user scripts. A user script with tool calls and no `finish` now fails. The repo fixture has a `finish` in every script (cli/tests/fixtures/triage_script.json). The CHANGELOG line "A custom `Model` must emit `Finish`" covers this case. | evals/src/mock.rs:53-86 | SAFE for repo; this is a user-facing change |

No provider leaves out `Finish` on a normal successful path.

### Strengths
- The change is small and in the right place. The no-Finish check comes after the ambiguous blank-id check and before the parse.
- The driver gives `Some(None)` only when `!finish_seen`. This branch runs only for an `Err` from `finish()`, and every such `Err` needs at least one tool call, so the mapping is never wrong.
- The tests reach the new code (proved above). The text-only case without `Finish` still gives `Ok` with `Stop` (model.rs:1288-1295), so (d) holds.
- (c) holds: an error that is not no-Finish and not Length/ContentFilter still goes to `AgentError::Other` (agent.rs:1534-1537).
- (e) holds. The mock fixes change only test helpers: core `run` (model.rs:1014-1021), `blank_tool_args_become_empty_object` (model.rs:991-993), anthropic `items_of` (translate/mod.rs:999-1004) and litellm `accumulated` (stream.rs:858-863). No assertion is weaker. Without the fix, the `run` users that expect parse errors would now get the no-Finish error and test the wrong thing. The anthropic and litellm helpers add `Finish` only when none was seen, and they read only `.items` or the tool tuples.

### Issues
#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)
1. **A user cancel during a tool-call stream now ends as a model failure, not as `RunError::Cancelled`.**
   - The `Model::invoke` contract says a model MUST NOT emit `Finish` on cancellation (model.rs:66-72). Every provider returns from its stream with no `Finish` when the token fires.
   - The driver does not check cancellation before it maps the error (agent.rs:1466-1539). It sees no `Finish` and yields `RunFailed(ToolCallsNotRun { finish_reason: None })` in the same poll.
